chapter: Predicate tests of the attacker models
label: tab:clause-tests
text: Each attacker model tested on each predicate of Table 1. A cell is yes when the predicate is true of the attacker model's own behaviour, rule when only a fixed rule its authors set makes it true, assumed when the attacker model takes the step but only its authors assume it, and no otherwise. Each property's row gives its mark: \propmet when every cell is yes, \propnone when every behaviour predicate is no, and \propstandin otherwise.

chapter: Supplementary material for the APT attacker model
label: tab:profile-sources
text: The sources that answered the two questions of Section 1 for each attack flow, grouped by attack profile (Table 1). The CTID description of every attack flow was read , with the analyst's notes on its steps where needed; the columns give what else was read, and a blank row needed nothing else. ATT | CK group is the group page read , and Threat report the report the attack flow cites.

chapter: Supplementary material for the APT attacker model
label: fig:profile-edges
text: Edges of the four attack profiles: each cell is an edge from the tactic of its row to the tactic of its column, darker where more of the attack profile's attack flows draw it. A cell above the diagonal runs forward in ATT | CK's order of tactics, and one below it back to an earlier tactic. Exfiltration is outlined where the attackers stole data, and Impact where they impeded systems (Table 1).

chapter: Supplementary material for the APT attacker model
label: tab:attack-action-times
text: Each tactic, in ATT | CK's order, with the attack action it runs (Figure 1), that attack action's time in MTDSim , which the baseline attacker takes, and the tactic's mean duration, which the APT attacker model takes instead. The exploit's time is its mean: it takes 0 to 9 s, by the vulnerability.

chapter: Supplementary material for the APT attacker model
label: tab:overlay-failure-rules
text: The rules of the failure matrix (Section 1). After a tactic's attack action fails, the first rule that applies to a candidate next tactic, from A down, gives its value. In ATT | CK's order, a tactic after Initial Access needs a foothold (Section 1). Stage is the next tactic's lifecycle stage against the failed tactic's.

chapter: Supplementary material for the APT attacker model
label: tab:value-bases

chapter: Supplementary material for the MTD evaluation
label: tab:mtdshield-configuration
text: MTDShield's settings in training, from the release's training script , and as run in Chapter 1 (Table 1). In both, it chooses among complete topology shuffle, IP shuffle, OS diversity and service diversity, or nothing; it is told the attacker's current attack action at every decision; and a deployment is forced after 2 000 s without one.

chapter: Supplementary material for the MTD evaluation
label: tab:disruption
text: The values of Figure 1, each with its 95 % confidence interval: attack actions blocked and time lost per MTD deployment at a deployment interval of 2 000 s, the APT attacker model averaged over x to x. Time lost is over the MTD deployments made while the same seed's run with no MTD is still going, which are at least 78 % of each cell's MTD deployments. A printed 1.000 is exact.

chapter: Supplementary material for the MTD evaluation
label: tab:eff-interval-values
text: NCR reduction for each MTD mechanism and deployment strategy against each attacker, at every deployment interval: the values of Figure 1, the APT attacker model averaged over x to x. An italic row is a layer's mean, the line the figure plots. Grey: the 95 % interval includes zero. Random, MTDShield's four: the random deployment strategy over the four MTD mechanisms MTDShield chooses from (Appendix 1).

label: tab:rank-one-intervals

chapter: Supplementary material for the MTD evaluation

text: NCR at the low end, the declared value and the high end of each mean duration's band (Table 1); the APT attacker model averaged over x to x, 400 runs per cell. Execution and Defense Impairment have half the 45 s mean duration, so moving the 45 s moves theirs too. Change: high end minus low end; bold, the largest. Every NCR's 95 % interval is within x.

chapter: Supplementary material for the MTD evaluation
label: tab:duration-ranking

Bold: rank 1, by Scott--Knott ESD. x: Spearman's rank correlation with the baseline attacker's NCR reductions; every 95 % interval lies within x and x.
